title: Teaser of my cyberpunk pixel-art game (still a work in progress)
author: Yigidus
selftext:
Here's a teaser of the 2D cyberpunk pixel-art action game I'm working on.



This isn't the official trailer. It's just a teaser test to show a bit more of the game. There's still a lot of work and polish ahead.



Steam page coming soon. For now, I'm posting progress on Instagram: u/cityofanimalsgame (more places coming later).



Any feedback is welcome!

comments.author: Significant_Tell407
comments.body: Can you talk about the pipeline you used for pixel art generations or yet another post with 0 fucking explanation.

replies.author: Yigidus
replies.body: Most characters start from my own sprites or detailed concept art, then get animated with PixelLab and cleaned up and customized by hand in Aseprite. Backgrounds and props are mostly code-drawn with Claude Code, then refined with very specific direction or by hand after a point, all locked to one color palette. I'm still learning how to do all this too.

replies.author: Yigidus
replies.body: Claude Code writes most of the code, but I direct everything and play-test every change myself. The first version of a mechanic usually works, but the feel almost never comes out right on the first try, so I keep tweaking timing, distances, sounds and so on until it feels good. So yes, I'm happy with it, but it still takes a lot of iteration.

replies.body: Thanks! PC comes first, but mobile might happen later if there's enough interest.

replies.author: Protocontext
replies.body: You should definitely consider including an iOS version at launch, or even releasing it on iOS first! I'm telling you from experience, games like this can sell like hotcakes on the App Store. Apple devices are incredibly capable when it comes to gaming, and pixel art games run beautifully on iPhones and iPads. I'm currently developing three games for iOS first, alongside several other apps I already have on the App Store, and if everything goes well, I'll bring them to Steam later. It's easier to publish, get valuable feedback through TestFlight or directly from App Store users, and optimize for a smaller range of devices. Plus, once your game runs smoothly on iPhones and iPads, getting it to run even better on PC should be much easier and require less work!

replies.author: Yigidus
replies.body: Thanks for the tip! For now it’s Steam first. The combat is built around keyboard/gamepad (cover, parry, aiming), so touch would need a lot of rework. Unity makes a port possible later though, so mobile isn’t off the table.
